title: Count in 2s, 5s and 10s
summary: Mix twos, fives and tens, count back, and spot a number you would not say.
subject: maths

difficultyRamp.within: Q1 counts back in twos from 20. Child subtracts 2, not 1. Q2 spots 16 in a fives count. Q3 uses 5 hands to make 25 fingers. Q4 reads 12 on a number line with no objects. Q5 finds 30 counting back in tens. Q6 picks two numbers you would not say in tens. Q7 matches 40 to a tens count. Q8 counts back in fives from 15. Q9 fills 70 on a hundred square. Q10 orders 20, 30, 40, 50.
difficultyRamp.versus: Easy uses pairs and tens pictures up to 50. Medium introduces fives, continuing a count, a missing 5s number and counting groups. Hard mixes steps, counts back, spots a number you would not say, uses a number line with no objects, and a short hands story. Hard is a new kind of thinking, not just bigger numbers.
